name: options-reeds-a
prompt: Output ONE image, 16:9. A contact sheet of FOUR separate paintings in a 2 by 2 grid, each the same size, separated by thin plain dark gutters; no labels, no letters, no numbers, no text anywhere. Each painting is a different concept for the same kind of view: the inside of one terrarium room inside a rugged, matte field device, seen straight on from a low eye height, wide, with a soft out-of-focus back and a sharp floor. In every painting the lowest third is a LOW, CALM, OPEN FLOOR running the full width: mostly short even moss or fine soil, plain and quiet, few pebbles, no litter or scree scattered over it, so that small creatures would read clearly on it; a thin dark soil strip along the very bottom edge; two small low foreground pieces sit at the front of the floor, one in the left third and one in the right third, each no taller than a tenth of the picture; all tall planting and every life-support fitting stands BEHIND the floor, in the back two thirds, never on the floor and never along the side edges as a hose or pipe running down a wall. Painted in a warm hand-crafted miniature-diorama finish: fine painterly grain, soft bokeh behind, believable materials, never photographic, never toon, never childish, no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow, no chrome, no alien tech, never a box or a cabinet. No creatures, no animals, no figures, no pool or pond, no open water, no cliff, no crag, no ledge. The four concepts must be clearly different from each other in palette, mood, light and fittings. The room is a reed and rush margin on dry damp ground. TOP LEFT: a marsh margin on a misty gold morning: backlit straw-gold reeds with rim-lit seed heads in pale haze; a thin cane-and-brass drip rail runs across the top of the back with small drips falling into the reeds; a small float gauge on a reed stake at the back right. TOP RIGHT: a sedge meadow just after rain under soft overcast light: silver-green sedges beaded with droplets, cool grey-green palette with a warm moss floor; a ceramic rain-catch funnel on a slim copper stand at the back left. BOTTOM LEFT: late-summer dry rushes in russet, ochre and straw under warm low wind-tossed light; a wicker-wrapped humidity cylinder standing at the back right among the rushes. BOTTOM RIGHT: a fen of deep green horsetail stems with banded joints and a few cattails, a blue-grey slate back, cool clear light with warm accents; a small brass drip reservoir hanging from a hook at the centre back.
